explanation: Gap of 290.3 MW: Top-down benchmarks (Cushman & Wakefield, JLL) measure Gross Facility Load (substation connected power) and aggregate captive sub-5 MW enterprise/banking facilities (e.g. SBI, RBI, HDFC legacy centers in Belapur and Mahape). Our dataset records confirmed critical IT load of commercial/hyperscale campuses.

Concordance within 0.7%: Dataset operational IT load (215.4 MW) closely aligns with C&W market benchmark (214.0 MW), reflecting high disclosure transparency across major colocation operators in Ambattur and Siruseri corridors.
Gap of 65.0 MW: Benchmarks count gross facility power and include older sub-5 MW telecom and enterprise server rooms in Okhla, Sector 18 Gurgaon, and Udyog Vihar below the dissertation threshold.

Gap of 70.5 MW: Difference reflects captive tech park server rooms, legacy IT labs (Electronic City and Whitefield), and sub-5 MW colocation modules not tracked as independent commercial hyperscale campuses.

Gap of 129.2 MW: The entire discrepancy is caused by undisclosed captive hyperscale capacity. AWS operates 3 Availability Zones (ap-south-2, live since Nov 2022) and Microsoft operates 3 Availability Zones (India South Central, live since Aug 2026). Neither operator discloses per-campus MW. These 5 campuses are tracked with status Operational, but MW is kept null rather than guessing.
Gap of 30.0 MW: Benchmark counts legacy Hinjewadi and Magarpatta enterprise data centers below 5 MW (e.g. Web Werks PUN-1 at 3.2 MW and older colocation modules).

Concordance: Dataset operational load (22.0 MW: CtrlS 16.0 MW + NTT 6.0 MW) matches the market benchmark exactly, representing the two commercial facilities currently live in Bengal Silicon Valley (New Town).
